advisories.title: @hono/node-server: Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic
advisories.chainAfter: ABSENT — @prisma/dev@0.24.17 (pinned by prisma@7.9.1) declares no @hono/node-server dependency in its package.json; the transitive chain is eliminated by upgrading the direct parent.
advisories.remediationStrategy: Phase B Option B (compatible direct-parent Prisma upgrade). Bumped prisma/@prisma/client/@prisma/adapter-mariadb from 7.8.0 → 7.9.1. New @prisma/dev=0.24.17 no longer references @hono/node-server.

advisories.chainAfter: ABSENT — same chain removal as advisory 1116281.
advisories.remediationStrategy: Phase B Option B (compatible direct-parent Prisma upgrade). Same remediation as 1116281.

advisories.title: Valibot: record() issue paths can make flatten() throw for inherited Object property names
advisories.remediationStrategy: Phase B Option B. valibot upgraded transitively from 1.2.0 to 1.4.2 via @prisma/dev@0.24.17. Validated patched range via npm registry metadata.

advisories.title: body-parser vulnerable to denial of service when invalid limit value silently disables size enforcement
advisories.remediationStrategy: Phase C Option 3 (precise pnpm override). express@5.2.1 declares body-parser@^2.2.1 which already admits 2.3.0, so an explicit root override selecting 2.3.0 is fully compatible and forced.

advisories.title: brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash
advisories.chainAfter: All edges rewritten to brace-expansion@5.0.8 via root override. minimatch 3/5/9 declare caret ranges ^1.1.0 and ^2.0.0 that do not include 5.0.8; pnpm still accepts the explicit root override and resolves the package graph to 5.0.8 across all minimatch paths.
advisories.remediationStrategy: Phase D. Global root override because (a) all three minimatch ranges required a single common patched target, (b) minimatch 3.x and 5.x/9.x declare non-overlapping ranges so a parent-qualified override cannot converge without an additional minimatch upgrade, and (c) brace-expansion@5.x keeps the same expand() API as 1.x/2.x (only adds maxLength option), so runtime compatibility holds. No package was pinned to a vulnerable version.
